narration.text: A kitchen nonprofit's restricted funds are released on 9 October as their terms are met: a cooler in service, a gift whose date a mailed amendment moved up, 6,300 dollars of meals money, 9,400 and 5,700 dollars of two grants, and two releases reported, while a van, a later date, 104 of 150 served and a consultant wait. This is a chore for the finance manager of a small community kitchen, a week after the quarter's close, who books the releases and files the funders' reports. On the bench, she found 7 of 7 eligible items, worth 74,600 dollars of the 74,600 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 10 traps, and she walked past 10. She took 3 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 3 hours, so she was about 64 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
